knowledge_gaps: The audit measures candidate-set sensitivity, but changing candidate distributions alone does not establish defective discrimination. Lexical candidates can differ in popularity, text coverage and actual relevance. Report these distributions and narrow causal interpretations; consider a lexical-versus-uniform comparison within the same frequency band.

Training-prefix targets may already have been supervised during fitting. Removing the target from inference input prevents direct input leakage but does not establish generalization. Also, full-training item frequencies include interactions occurring after historical audit endpoints; explicitly describe this as retrospective checkpoint diagnosis.

Production integration remains underspecified: the current adapter previously lacked category identity, replay batches and exported-loader access. The pseudocode also passes full sequence features and a flat candidate list to a position-wise scoring interface without specifying tensor shapes or gathering the MASK feature.

Reproducibility requires exact TF-IDF settings, metadata-to-item mapping, text normalization, feature cap, candidate seed derivation, history-length strata, bootstrap count and aggregation rules. Define how fewer than 500 positive-similarity neighbors are handled when at least 99 remain.

The 15-second GPU cap does not bound lexical preparation, checkpoint loading or total diagnostic runtime. Cache the single MASK representation per endpoint, use sparse target-to-catalog retrieval, and predeclare completion rules so timeouts do not silently change paired comparison populations.

Three draws and at most 32 users per category provide limited evidence, especially after availability filtering and stratification. Report candidate overlap, pool sizes, directional hit flips and common-user denominators; repeated draws are not independent users. Any four-category macro diagnostic needs explicit equal-category aggregation.

Originality 4/10 is reasonable. Potential 7/10 is optimistic without a defined decision the audit will inform, while difficulty 3/10 understates the unresolved serving, routing and metadata integration. Restore production diagnostic coverage first; no supplied evidence justifies replacing the idea with a training modification.

follow_up_queries.reason: Clarify what candidate-regime differences can establish and identify controls for popularity, missing text and unverified negative relevance.
follow_up_queries.query: In offline sequential recommendation evaluation, how should uniform, popularity-matched and text-similar candidate sets be compared for one fixed recommender checkpoint? Find methodological work on candidate-distribution confounding, false negatives and common-support comparisons, including Krichene and Rendle's On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve the concrete scoring and retrieval details needed for a reproducible adapter without changing the deployed single BERT4Rec predictor.
follow_up_queries.query: For a left-padded BERT4Rec diagnostic using log2feats outputs shaped B x L x D and position-wise candidate scoring, how should appended-MASK features and candidate tensors be gathered and broadcast? Also find scikit-learn guidance for deterministic sparse TF-IDF target-to-catalog cosine retrieval, including empty text, zero similarity, top-k ties and avoiding dense catalog-by-catalog matrices.

follow_up_queries.reason: Separate retrospective in-sample diagnosis from temporal generalization and specify uncertainty with repeated candidate draws.
follow_up_queries.query: What methodological guidance applies when auditing a trained sequential recommender on historical training-prefix targets it may have memorized? Investigate retrospective versus time-local item-frequency statistics, training-data reuse limitations, and paired user-cluster bootstrap comparisons with repeated negative-candidate draws and regime-dependent missingness.
